summary.en: Select each suffix minimum with few exchanges while keeping comparisons and stability claims separate.
summary.bn: বাকি অংশের সর্বনিম্ন মান খুঁজে বসাও, আর কম swap-এর সঙ্গে stability-এর পার্থক্য দেখো।

notes: C17 baseline; general algorithm bounds treat input size as variable.

examples.title: Order five marks, including a tie
examples.explanationHtml: The first minimum is 1 and later selections finish 1 3 3 5 7. Only two nontrivial exchanges are needed.

examples.title: Sort numbers entered at the keyboard
examples.explanationHtml: The suffix-minimum scans accept negatives without any special slot encoding. Both copies of -2 remain first.

examples.title: Use sorted neighbours to find distinct marks
examples.explanationHtml: Selection makes equal scores neighbours, allowing one forward group count to report three different values.

examples.title: Count comparisons and real exchanges
examples.explanationHtml: Ascending selection input needs ten comparisons but no real exchange. The suffix scan length does not depend on movement.

practice.title: Find the suffix minimum position
practice.statementHtml: Model one selection scan without swapping: display Enter n, then n values:, accept n = 0..64 and keys -99..99, then display Enter start: and read start = 0..n. Print min index = I for the first minimum in [start,n), or -1 for an empty suffix.
hints: Retain the earlier candidate when an equal key appears.

practice.title: Measure selection exchanges
practice.statementHtml: Run swapping selection sort and count only exchanges between different positions. The input is n (0..64) followed by n keys (-99..99); first print Enter n, then n values:. Finish with swaps = S and skip self-swaps.
hints: One completed minimum scan permits at most one real exchange.

practice.title: Explain the Selection Sort invariant
practice.statementHtml: For Selection Sort, state what stays true as the main process repeats. Explain the start, preservation and completed result.
hints: Use the changing boundaries and the processed region in this method.
practice.answerHtml:
Inside the scan, min identifies a smallest value among suffix positions i through j - 1. Initialising min to i establishes the claim before the first comparison. Comparing a[j] either finds a smaller candidate or leaves the existing one valid. At the scan's end, min identifies a minimum of the entire suffix.

The outer invariant says the prefix below i is sorted and contains the smallest i input values. Installing the suffix minimum extends that prefix without losing any value. Each outer pass increases i, so the unfinished suffix shrinks until only one value remains. The final array is a sorted permutation of the input.

practice.title: Derive the resource cost of Selection Sort
practice.statementHtml: Distinguish the fixed triangular comparison count from the input-dependent exchange count.
hints: Count the work from this algorithm rather than naming a class alone.
practice.answerHtml: All input orders make Θ(n²) comparisons. At most n - 1 nontrivial swaps give O(n) exchanges, while auxiliary storage is Θ(1). Few swaps do not reduce the total asymptotic time because comparison scans still dominate. Ordinary selection sort is in-place and unstable. A stable shift-based variant should be analysed separately rather than assigned the same exchange count.

quiz.prompt: What does min store during selection sort?
options: An index of a smallest scanned value
quiz.explanation: The final exchange needs the original position of the selected record.

quiz.prompt: How many comparisons occur on an already sorted n-element array?
quiz.explanation: Every suffix must still be scanned for a smaller value.

quiz.prompt: With self-swaps skipped, what is the maximum number of exchanges?
quiz.explanation: Each useful outer pass performs at most one exchange.

quiz.prompt: What happens to [2A,2B,1] after selecting its first minimum?
quiz.explanation: Moving 2A to the far end jumps over equal-key 2B.

options: After every comparison regardless of outcome
quiz.explanation: The next suffix begins at the new i.

quiz.prompt: Why can low swap count still accompany quadratic time?
quiz.explanation: Comparisons sum to a triangular quadratic count.

quiz.prompt: Which movement can make a selection variant stable?
options: Reverse the prefix after each pass
Remove the minimum and shift intervening records right
quiz.explanation: Shifting preserves the relative order of the crossed records.

quiz.prompt: Which minimum index is selected from [4,2,1]?
How many comparisons scan a selection suffix of length four?
quiz.explanation: The initial candidate needs comparison against three other positions.

quiz.prompt: Which array follows the first selection exchange on [4,2,1]?
quiz.explanation: The selected minimum 1 trades positions with 4.

keyPoints.en: Select the minimum before making a swap.
keyPoints.bn: আগে পুরো অংশের ছোট মান খোঁজো, তারপর swap করো।

keyPoints.en: The prefix becomes final one position at a time.
keyPoints.bn: বামের সাজানো অংশ প্রতি পাসে এক ঘর বাড়ে।
যে ক্রমেই থাকুক, তুলনা quadratic সংখ্যক লাগে।
নিজের সঙ্গে swap বাদ দিলে আসল অদলবদল কম হয়।

keyPoints.en: A distant exchange can reverse equal records.
keyPoints.bn: দূরের swap-এ সমান record-এর ক্রম উল্টে যেতে পারে।
